messages:
Maya: Quick thread — I'm proposing an 'opportunistic downshift' routing policy. When a request would push a customer's short-term token spend estimate over their soft cap or when we detect a large single-request token estimate, route to a cheaper compatible variant (same decoder shape ideally) rather than queuing or failing. Goals: keep p95 latency / correctness similar, reduce surprise billing, expose an opt-out toggle in Console. Thoughts?

Sam: what signals are we using to decide 'push over cap'? per-request token_estimate? rolling 1h token burn? both?

Maya: +both. primary signal = per-request token_estimate + projected 5m burn from active sessions. fallback to rolling-hour when we can't estimate. priority = preservation of quality > cost for higher tiers.

Ashley: billing note: we must surface the exact billing delta customers will see when routed. console should show "estimated tokens billed" + "variant cost multiplier" before they opt-in. If we silently change model we need consent for enterprise.

Liam: question about KV cache / prefix caching: cheaper variant might not have identical KV cache compatibility. If we switch mid-session we could lose cached context and spike latency. Need a rule to avoid switching after cache warm-up or during active streaming.

Dez: UX + telemetry: Console panel idea — new column on Route config: "Opportunistic downshift" with toggles: off / opportunistic / aggressive. Tooltip shows expected cost delta for a sample 1k-token request. Telemetry events to emit: `downshift_evaluated`, `downshift_executed`, `downshift_reverted`, with labels: customer_tier, region, route, from_variant, to_variant, token_estimate, decision_reason.

Priya: rollout plan suggestion — staged canary: 1) internal-only simulate decisions offline for 48h and compute false-positive/neg rates using labeled prompts, 2) 1% of Free tier (aggressive) + 0.5% of Startup (opportunistic) for 72h, 3) widen to 10%/5% if regressions < thresholds. Metrics to assert: quality-regression (BLEU/ROUGE or eval set accept rate) < 1.5% relative, p95 latency change < 10%, average token-cost reduction >= 12% for targeted population, customer complaints/tickets <= baseline + 2.

Sam: do we want a per-request override header? e.g., `x-redwood-prefer-quality: true|false` so SDKs can ask to bypass for important calls.

Maya: yes — header + Console route-level default. Also a per-customer whitelist for guaranteed full fidelity.

Liam: on implementation: runtime needs to expose `can_variant_swap(session_state)` that checks KV cache compatibility and sequence-length heuristics. Also a fast cost-model: cost_est = tokens * variant_price_per_token + model_switch_penalty_est. Keep the model_switch_penalty configurable.

Dez: sample routing policy snippet for the API config — please copy/paste and iterate:

```json
{
  "policy_name": "opportunistic_downshift_v1",
  "conditions": [
    { "signal": "per_request_token_estimate", "op": ">", "value": 1500 },
    { "signal": "projected_5m_burn_pct", "op": ">=", "value": 0.9 }
  ],
  "decision_strategy": "cost_first_if_tier<=startup_else_quality",
  "variants_order": ["gpt-7b-q8", "gptx-13b-q4", "gpt-34b"],
  "safety_checks": ["kv_cache_compatible", "no_stream_mid_swap"]
}
```

Ashley: make sure the Console shows a pre-commit simulation: "simulate on sample traffic" that runs the policy against last 24h traffic and shows estimated delta cost + quality signal. That will reduce support load.

Priya: rollout safety gates: auto-rollback if daily customers affected > 0.5% OR if quality-regression > 2% for top 50 customers by revenue. Also require legal sign-off for enterprise global rollout.

Sam: telem question — do we emit cost-savings per-request to billing or just aggregate? prefer aggregate to avoid per-request billing drift in invoice.

Maya: aggregate only for billing. but per-request events need to exist in obs for debugging. billing team will calculate final cents at day boundary.

deploy-bot: canary created: opportunistic-downshift-v1 -> env=canary, subset=1% Free, 0.5% Startup (1723456798) :rocket:

observability-bot: dashboard template `dash/opportunistic-downshift` created. panels: downshift_rate, avg_cost_saved_per_1k_tokens, quality_regression_estimate, p95_latency_delta. link: https://dash.internal/redwood/opportunistic-downshift

Sam: one more: need an escape hatch in runtime: `runtime.set_policy_mode(route, 'monitor-only')` so Console toggle doesn't flip logic mid-canary.

Maya: good call. I'll sketch the RFC today with docs for SDK header, Console mockups, telemetry event schema, and rollout timeline. If no objections I'll open the RFC and tag infra / billing / legal.

Ashley: +1 — please include a sample invoice diff example in RFC so sales/ae know how to explain to customers.

Liam: +1 from runtime side, will prototype `can_variant_swap(session)` by EOD tomorrow.

Dez: I'll design the Console mockup and simulation button.

Priya: I'll draft the GA criteria and rollback thresholds.

Maya: thanks all. posting RFC in ~2h. :seedling:
